must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge deal team (Jay Cho)
**Re:** Departures from Buyer Playbook and recommended pushback
**Status of Seller material:** Other side's draft. Labels such as "agreed", "settled", "considered adequate" and "fair and balanced" are the Seller's characterisations only and bind nothing. Note also the Disclosure Letter is dated 22 September 2026 – six weeks stale as at today (6 November 2026) – so a bring-down will be needed in any event.

A preliminary observation: the Seller's cover note and the Disclosure Letter pull in opposite directions. The cover note minimises almost every issue; the Disclosure Letter itself candidly records that Bluefen consent is **not** obtained, Riverlark is **not** repaid, the DD-005 bonuses are **not** in the funds flow, and title rests on an internal register. We should use the Seller's own disclosures against the Seller's own drafting positions.

---

## 1. Liability architecture (Clauses 12, 13, 9.3, 12.8, 20.5)

### 1.1 General warranty cap – Seller: 20% / AUD 4.8m
- **Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6.0m. 20% is a conditional fallback **only** with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft. None has been given.
- **Departure:** Seller has simply asserted our fallback as the "negotiated" figure. It is not negotiated.
- **Pushback:** Reinstate 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not trade on the cap until Amelia Frost has given written authority for a specific draft. Internally, do not treat the 20% figure as having been conceded by anyone on our side.

### 1.2 Thresholds – Seller: de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only recovery
- **Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar** (tipping) recovery once the basket is exceeded.
- **Departure:** Three separate moves against us: de minimis 5x ours, basket 5x ours, and a deductible rather than tipping basket. On a AUD 24m deal, a AUD 250k deductible with a AUD 25k per-claim floor would filter out most realistic warranty claims entirely.
- **Pushback:** Revert all three to playbook. If any movement is ever contemplated, the deductible-vs-tipping point is the most valuable and should be the last to go, not the first.

### 1.3 Time limits – Seller: 18 months; "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"
- **Playbook:** 24 months for general claims; 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- **Departure:** (a) Again asserting our unauthorised fallback as agreed. (b) The second sentence is the more dangerous one: a default rule that every limitation applies to every Claim unless carved out expressly. Combined with 1.4–1.5 below, this would collapse Fundamental/Title, Tax, IP, payment covenants and specific indemnities into the 18-month/20%/basket regime.
- **Pushback:** 24 months. Delete the "applies to all Claims" default and replace with the opposite default: limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims and only where expressly stated.

### 1.4 Fundamental / Title claims – Seller: same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity"
- **Playbook:** Separate regime – 100% of price cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.
- **Departure:** Fundamental. If title to the shares fails, a AUD 4.8m recovery (less a AUD 250k deductible) on a AUD 24m purchase is unacceptable. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason.
- **Pushback:** Reject outright. Insert separate Fundamental Warranty definitions (title, capacity, authority, no encumbrances, share capital) with 100% cap, six-year period, no basket/de minimis, and express exclusion from Clause 8.3 and the Schedule 7 disclosure mechanics.

### 1.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance "apply to all Claims of any nature" (9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- **Playbook:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum extent enforceable. Nobody on our side may waive this. Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories kept separate with no hidden general-regime override.
- **Departure:** "All Claims of any nature" is a universal override. On its face it would (i) cap and time-bar fraud claims, (ii) sweep in the Ironquay indemnity, Riverlark repayment obligations, leakage/price-adjustment claims and any Tax or IP indemnity, and (iii) make the non-reliance clause operate even where the Seller has deliberately concealed. Whether a fraud cap is enforceable is beside the point – we should not be arguing it later.
- **Pushback:** Insert an overriding carve-out clause at the top of Clause 12: nothing in the SPA limits or excludes liability for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct by the Seller or Company, and nothing in Clause 12 applies to Fundamental Warranty Claims, Tax Claims, IP Claims, specific indemnities, price-adjustment/leakage claims or covenant claims except as expressly stated in a schedule for each. Delete "of any nature" wording in 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5.

### 1.6 Tax / IP – Seller: "settled under the general regime"
- **Playbook:** Tax and IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
- **Departure:** The Seller is attempting to close these by assertion, folding them into 20%/18 months/deductible.
- **Pushback:** State in reply that Tax and IP remain open and are not governed by Clause 12 pending agreement of a separate Tax Indemnity/Tax Warranty regime and IP warranty/indemnity package. Do not counter with a figure yet; we have no instruction on a number.

---

## 2. Disclosure and knowledge

### 2.1 General disclosure of the data room and public registers (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2)
- **Playbook:** Specific, fair disclosure only. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Departure:** Paragraph 1.1 discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in" the data room (DD-002 to DD-012), and 1.2 adds statutory registers and all publicly searchable records. This is exactly the deemed-disclosure model the playbook rejects: everything in a document index becomes a defence to every warranty, regardless of whether a reasonable buyer would have identified the issue.
- **Pushback:** Delete 1.1 and 1.2. Replace with a "fair disclosure" standard: a matter is disclosed only if set out in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its effect on the warranty. Specific data room documents may be referenced by number against specific warranties. Public registers should be limited, if at all, to ASIC company extract and PPSR searches actually conducted and dated.
- **Note on 1.4 (no admission):** Acceptable in principle, but it cannot sit alongside 1.1. The Seller cannot both disclose "everything" as a shield and admit nothing. Our fair-disclosure standard should make clear that a matter is only disclosed if its nature and consequence are disclosed, not merely its existence.

### 2.2 Buyer knowledge bar (Clause 8.3)
- **Playbook:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier must reference named seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Departure:** Clause 8.3 bars any claim for a matter of which "the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records". "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge test – it bars claims for things we did **not** know but theoretically could have found. Combined with 2.1, it removes the warranties as a risk-allocation tool: every disclosed-by-index matter becomes "discoverable". It also extends to advisers' knowledge, which raises evidentiary problems and potential privilege disputes.
- **Pushback:** Delete 8.3 entirely. If the Seller insists on any knowledge concept, limit to the **Seller's** knowledge warranties ("so far as the Seller is aware"), defined by named individuals (e.g. the Seller's nominated directors and the Company CEO/CFO) after due and careful enquiry. Expressly state that Buyer knowledge, actual or constructive, does not reduce or exclude any claim, and in any event never Fundamental, fraud or specific indemnity claims.

---

## 3. Conditions and completion deliverables

### 3.1 Bluefen consent (Clauses 3 / 6.3)
- **Playbook:** Effective consent **and** evidence that the conditions to the consent are satisfied, before Completion. Not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer.
- **Facts (Seller's own Disclosure Letter, para 2):** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue, ~30% of the business. Change-control consent under clause 11.2 is subject to conditions in 11.3. **No final written consent and no evidence of condition satisfaction** is in the data room.
- **Departure:** Seller's cover note says the matter is "addressed", then offers only reasonable endeavours and a deemed-satisfied-on-delivery trigger. Delivery of a conditional consent whose conditions are unmet is no consent; if Bluefen then terminates, we have bought a business missing 30% of its revenue with the condition "satisfied".
- **Pushback:** Condition precedent in the Buyer's favour: (a) written, unconditional consent from Bluefen under clause 11.2 in a form approved by the Buyer (acting reasonably), **and** (b) written evidence, acceptable to the Buyer, that each condition in clause 11.3 has been satisfied or irrevocably waived by Bluefen. Seller obligation at "all reasonable endeavours" or "best endeavours", with a Buyer-only waiver right and a long-stop. Delete the deemed-satisfaction language. Consider a price-protection mechanism (retention/escrow or specific indemnity) if Completion is to occur before clause 11.3 conditions are fully evidenced – but only with Amelia Frost's instruction.

### 3.2 Riverlark Bank facility (Clauses 2 / 7)
- **Playbook:** Current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion. A post-Completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking **plus** Amelia Frost approval.
- **Facts (Disclosure Letter para 3):** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; change-of-control clause 8.1; discharge clause 9.2; facility not repaid; no final discharge of security.
- **Departure:** Seller proposes a release "to be provided following Completion". This is a debt-free/cash-free deal: we would complete with AUD 3.2m of secured debt still on the Company, the bank holding security over assets we have just paid for, a change-of-control default live under clause 8.1, and the Seller holding the price. The "approximately" figure also suggests no current payout letter.
- **Pushback:** (a) Current payout letter from Riverlark dated not more than 2–3 business days before Completion, figure to be a line item in the funds flow deducted from the price. (b) Buyer pays Riverlark directly at Completion from the Completion payment. (c) Executed deeds of release/discharge of all security (and PPSR release undertakings) delivered at Completion, held in escrow pending payment. (d) Riverlark's written confirmation that clause 8.1 is waived or spent on repayment. Reject the post-Completion release. If the Seller cannot deliver releases at Completion, do not proceed on that basis without an irrevocable bank undertaking **and** Amelia Frost's written approval.

### 3.3 Funds flow and DD-005 bonuses
- **Playbook:** AUD 420,000 bonuses plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or Seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Facts (Disclosure Letter para 5):** AUD 420k conditional Completion bonuses; **not** in the draft funds flow; disclosure silent on payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs.
- **Departure:** The Seller's note says the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" but simultaneously keeps them out of the funds flow. If they are not in the funds flow and not otherwise Seller-funded, the Company (i.e. the Buyer post-Completion) pays them. This is a transaction cost triggered by the Seller's sale and belongs with the Seller. The reference to "agreed price mechanics" should be rejected – nothing is agreed.
- **Pushback:** Treat DD-005 bonuses as Transaction Bonuses within the Debt/Transaction Costs definition: AUD 420,000 **plus** superannuation, payroll tax and any other employer on-costs (to be quantified by the Seller before signing), either (i) deducted from the price in the funds flow and paid by the Company at Completion out of Seller proceeds, or (ii) paid by the Seller directly with a Seller indemnity for any shortfall and on-costs. Require the Seller to confirm whether any additional retention or change-of-control payments exist beyond DD-005.

### 3.4 Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
- These are disclosed as notification-only / assignment restriction only. We should not accept the Seller's characterisation without reading the clauses ourselves (the Seller's 1.4 reservation applies here too). **Action:** DD confirmation whether a share sale triggers either a landlord consent or a Mossvale change-of-control right; if either does, add to the Conditions/Completion deliverables. If not, require the notifications to be given pre-Completion with evidence.

---

## 4. Specific risk items

### 4.1 Ironquay IP (Clause 11.1)
- **Playbook:** Broaden the narrow indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- **Facts (Disclosure Letter para 4):** DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180k open; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room; DD-010 is not bank verification.
- **Departure:** The Seller's indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment. The real exposure is not the AUD 180k – it is that the Company may not own the SOW3 deliverables at all until payment clears, and any loss from non-ownership (customer claims, re-development cost, inability to license) is uncapped by the payment amount.
- **Pushback:** (a) Pre-Completion cure: Seller to procure cleared payment of all SOW3 fees and deliver Ironquay's written receipt plus a confirmatory IP assignment of SOW3 Project Materials as a Completion deliverable. (b) Indemnity broadened to cover all Loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or any third-party claim to, the SOW3 Project Materials or any other Ironquay deliverable, including any further amounts Ironquay claims, not merely the SOW3 payment. (c) Indemnity outside Clause 12 limitations. (d) Neither side should assume the AUD 180k is correct – require a reconciled statement from Ironquay.

### 4.2 Export / privacy incident (DD-006; Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6)
- **Playbook:** Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- **Facts (Disclosure Letter para 6):** Download link sent to unintended external address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps); unknown whether accessed; investigation preliminary; no loss stated.
- **Departure:** Seller's cover note calls it "preliminary" and "not expected to be material" – but its own Disclosure Letter says the material cannot establish access, scope or notification requirement. "Not expected to be material" is a conclusion the Seller's own evidence does not support (nor contradict).
- **Pushback (without asserting a breach):** (a) Pre-Completion covenant to preserve all logs, link access records and correspondence, and to complete the investigation (including link revocation confirmation and access-log analysis) with written updates to the Buyer. (b) Bring-down of the disclosure at Completion. (c) Specific indemnity for Loss arising from the DD-006 incident (regulator action, notification costs, third-party claims), outside Clause 12 caps and time limits, with a specific indemnity period of at least six years. (d) Do not propose a price adjustment or quantify a demand – there is no basis for a number yet. (e) Warranty that no other similar incidents have occurred in the last three years.

### 4.3 Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011) – AUD 330,000
- **Playbook:** Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Facts (Disclosure Letter para 8):** Three related renewals of AUD 110k each; the disclosure does not say whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Departure:** Seller's cover note asserts "ordinary-course operating costs"; the Disclosure Letter expressly declines to say so. Mild inconsistency, not yet a dispute.
- **Pushback:** Do **not** propose a Debt classification or price deduction now. Instead request: renewal dates and terms, termination rights and notice periods, whether any amount is accrued or prepaid at the locked-box/Completion accounts date, and whether the three are a single commitment split or genuinely separate. Decide classification once answered. If they are accrued pre-Completion but unpaid, they belong in Working Capital/Debt under the completion mechanism; if genuinely forward-looking ordinary course, they do not.

### 4.4 Title (DD-012)
- **Playbook:** Independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; the DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- **Facts (Disclosure Letter para 10):** Title is evidenced by the Company's own share register; the Seller expressly notes the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Departure:** The Seller's note treats DD-012 as sufficient. A company's own register is maintained by the company (i.e. by the Seller's appointees) and is prima facie evidence only.
- **Pushback / DD actions:** (a) Current ASIC company extract showing Harbourglass as sole member and matching share capital. (b) PPSR search against the Company and against Harbourglass for security over the shares (Riverlark security in particular). (c) Copies of all share certificates, transfer history and board minutes approving the register entries. (d) Harbourglass's own constitutional documents and board/shareholder resolutions approving the sale (capacity and authority). (e) Full Fundamental Warranties (title, no encumbrances, capacity, authority, share capital, no options/convertibles) on the separate regime at 1.4 above.

---

## 5. Points where the Seller's documents are helpful to us

Worth noting so we do not negotiate against ourselves:
- The Disclosure Letter is candid on the factual gaps (Bluefen, Riverlark, DD-005, Ironquay, DD-006, title). We should quote these back in our mark-up as the justification for conditions and indemnities.
- Paragraph 11 (Reservation) confirms no approvals or negotiation positions are embedded. Equally, nothing in the Seller's cover note is "agreed".
- Paragraph 1.4 (no admission) is standard; we can live with it once 1.1/1.2 are removed.

---

## 6. Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Our response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | General cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | Revert to 25% / AUD 6.0m. 20% only on Amelia Frost written authority – none given. |
| 2 | Thresholds | DM 25k / basket 250k / deductible | Revert to DM 5k / basket 50k / first-dollar. |
| 3 | Claims period | 18 months; limitations apply to all Claims by default | 24 months; limitations apply only where expressly stated. |
| 4 | Fundamental/Title | Same as general | Separate regime: 100% cap, 6+ years, no basket/DM/knowledge bar. |
| 5 | Universal limitation / non-reliance | Applies to all Claims of any nature | Overriding fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out; Tax, IP, indemnities, covenants, price adjustment outside Clause 12. |
| 6 | Tax / IP | "Settled under general regime" | Remain OPEN; separate regimes to be negotiated; propose no number yet. |
| 7 | Disclosure | Whole data room + public registers | Delete; fair, specific disclosure only. |
| 8 | Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Blanket bar incl. "discoverable" | Delete; Seller knowledge qualifiers only with named persons + reasonable enquiry; never for title/capacity/fraud/indemnities. |
| 9 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours; satisfied on delivery | CP: unconditional consent **and** evidence of 11.3 conditions satisfied, Buyer-approved form, Buyer-only waiver. |
| 10 | Riverlark | Release post-Completion | Current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, releases delivered at Completion. Post-Completion release only with irrevocable bank undertaking + Amelia Frost approval. |
| 11 | DD-005 bonuses | Not itemised; "matter for Seller" | AUD 420k + on-costs as a specific line item deducted from price or Seller-funded with indemnity. |
| 12 | Ironquay | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment | Pre-Completion cure (payment + receipt + confirmatory assignment); broadened indemnity for non-ownership loss, outside Clause 12. AUD 180k to be reconciled. |
| 13 | DD-006 incident | "Not expected to be material" | Log preservation, completed investigation, bring-down, specific indemnity outside caps. No breach assumed; no number proposed. |
| 14 | Sandbar renewals | Ordinary course | Assess only; request terms; no Debt classification or deduction yet. |
| 15 | Title | DD-012 register | Independent evidence: ASIC extract, PPSR, certificates, Seller authority resolutions. |
| 16 | Lease / Mossvale | Notification only | Verify clauses ourselves; notifications given pre-Completion with evidence. |
| 17 | Disclosure Letter date | 22 Sep 2026 | Require updated letter and bring-down at signing and Completion. |

**Immediate next steps:**
1. Prepare a mark-up implementing items 1–8 (liability and disclosure architecture) – these are the structural points and should go back as a package, not piecemeal.
2. Issue a DD request list covering items 9–16 (Bluefen 11.3 evidence, Riverlark payout, DD-005 on-costs, Ironquay reconciliation, DD-006 log preservation, Sandbar terms, ASIC/PPSR, lease and Mossvale clauses).
3. Brief Amelia Frost that the Seller has pre-emptively asserted both of our unauthorised fallbacks (20% cap, 18 months) and that we are holding at playbook; no concession to be made on either without her written instruction identifying the draft.
4. Flag in our cover reply that nothing in the Seller's package is agreed, Tax and IP remain open, and the Disclosure Letter will need to be re-dated and brought down.

## 1. Liability architecture (Clauses 12, 13, 9.3, 12.8, 20.5)

### 1.1 General warranty cap – Seller: 20% / AUD 4.8m
- **Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6.0m. 20% is a conditional fallback **only** with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft. None has been given.
- **Departure:** Seller has simply asserted our fallback as the "negotiated" figure. It is not negotiated.
- **Pushback:** Reinstate 25% / AUD 6,000,000. Do not trade on the cap until Amelia Frost has given written authority for a specific draft. Internally, do not treat the 20% figure as having been conceded by anyone on our side.

### 1.2 Thresholds – Seller: de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only recovery
- **Playbook:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar** (tipping) recovery once the basket is exceeded.
- **Departure:** Three separate moves against us: de minimis 5x ours, basket 5x ours, and a deductible rather than tipping basket. On a AUD 24m deal, a AUD 250k deductible with a AUD 25k per-claim floor would filter out most realistic warranty claims entirely.
- **Pushback:** Revert all three to playbook. If any movement is ever contemplated, the deductible-vs-tipping point is the most valuable and should be the last to go, not the first.

### 1.3 Time limits – Seller: 18 months; "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"
- **Playbook:** 24 months for general claims; 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- **Departure:** (a) Again asserting our unauthorised fallback as agreed. (b) The second sentence is the more dangerous one: a default rule that every limitation applies to every Claim unless carved out expressly. Combined with 1.4–1.5 below, this would collapse Fundamental/Title, Tax, IP, payment covenants and specific indemnities into the 18-month/20%/basket regime.
- **Pushback:** 24 months. Delete the "applies to all Claims" default and replace with the opposite default: limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims and only where expressly stated.

### 1.4 Fundamental / Title claims – Seller: same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity"
- **Playbook:** Separate regime – 100% of price cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and any knowledge bar.
- **Departure:** Fundamental. If title to the shares fails, a AUD 4.8m recovery (less a AUD 250k deductible) on a AUD 24m purchase is unacceptable. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason.
- **Pushback:** Reject outright. Insert separate Fundamental Warranty definitions (title, capacity, authority, no encumbrances, share capital) with 100% cap, six-year period, no basket/de minimis, and express exclusion from Clause 8.3 and the Schedule 7 disclosure mechanics.

### 1.5 Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance "apply to all Claims of any nature" (9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- **Playbook:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance to the maximum extent enforceable. Nobody on our side may waive this. Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories kept separate with no hidden general-regime override.
- **Departure:** "All Claims of any nature" is a universal override. On its face it would (i) cap and time-bar fraud claims, (ii) sweep in the Ironquay indemnity, Riverlark repayment obligations, leakage/price-adjustment claims and any Tax or IP indemnity, and (iii) make the non-reliance clause operate even where the Seller has deliberately concealed. Whether a fraud cap is enforceable is beside the point – we should not be arguing it later.
- **Pushback:** Insert an overriding carve-out clause at the top of Clause 12: nothing in the SPA limits or excludes liability for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct by the Seller or Company, and nothing in Clause 12 applies to Fundamental Warranty Claims, Tax Claims, IP Claims, specific indemnities, price-adjustment/leakage claims or covenant claims except as expressly stated in a schedule for each. Delete "of any nature" wording in 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5.

### 1.6 Tax / IP – Seller: "settled under the general regime"
- **Playbook:** Tax and IP terms remain OPEN; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution.
- **Departure:** The Seller is attempting to close these by assertion, folding them into 20%/18 months/deductible.
- **Pushback:** State in reply that Tax and IP remain open and are not governed by Clause 12 pending agreement of a separate Tax Indemnity/Tax Warranty regime and IP warranty/indemnity package. Do not counter with a figure yet; we have no instruction on a number.

## 2. Disclosure and knowledge

### 2.1 General disclosure of the data room and public registers (Schedule 7; Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2)
- **Playbook:** Specific, fair disclosure only. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Departure:** Paragraph 1.1 discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in" the data room (DD-002 to DD-012), and 1.2 adds statutory registers and all publicly searchable records. This is exactly the deemed-disclosure model the playbook rejects: everything in a document index becomes a defence to every warranty, regardless of whether a reasonable buyer would have identified the issue.
- **Pushback:** Delete 1.1 and 1.2. Replace with a "fair disclosure" standard: a matter is disclosed only if set out in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its effect on the warranty. Specific data room documents may be referenced by number against specific warranties. Public registers should be limited, if at all, to ASIC company extract and PPSR searches actually conducted and dated.
- **Note on 1.4 (no admission):** Acceptable in principle, but it cannot sit alongside 1.1. The Seller cannot both disclose "everything" as a shield and admit nothing. Our fair-disclosure standard should make clear that a matter is only disclosed if its nature and consequence are disclosed, not merely its existence.

### 2.2 Buyer knowledge bar (Clause 8.3)
- **Playbook:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier must reference named seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Departure:** Clause 8.3 bars any claim for a matter of which "the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records". "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge test – it bars claims for things we did **not** know but theoretically could have found. Combined with 2.1, it removes the warranties as a risk-allocation tool: every disclosed-by-index matter becomes "discoverable". It also extends to advisers' knowledge, which raises evidentiary problems and potential privilege disputes.
- **Pushback:** Delete 8.3 entirely. If the Seller insists on any knowledge concept, limit to the **Seller's** knowledge warranties ("so far as the Seller is aware"), defined by named individuals (e.g. the Seller's nominated directors and the Company CEO/CFO) after due and careful enquiry. Expressly state that Buyer knowledge, actual or constructive, does not reduce or exclude any claim, and in any event never Fundamental, fraud or specific indemnity claims.

## 3. Conditions and completion deliverables

### 3.1 Bluefen consent (Clauses 3 / 6.3)
- **Playbook:** Effective consent **and** evidence that the conditions to the consent are satisfied, before Completion. Not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer.
- **Facts (Seller's own Disclosure Letter, para 2):** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue, ~30% of the business. Change-control consent under clause 11.2 is subject to conditions in 11.3. **No final written consent and no evidence of condition satisfaction** is in the data room.
- **Departure:** Seller's cover note says the matter is "addressed", then offers only reasonable endeavours and a deemed-satisfied-on-delivery trigger. Delivery of a conditional consent whose conditions are unmet is no consent; if Bluefen then terminates, we have bought a business missing 30% of its revenue with the condition "satisfied".
- **Pushback:** Condition precedent in the Buyer's favour: (a) written, unconditional consent from Bluefen under clause 11.2 in a form approved by the Buyer (acting reasonably), **and** (b) written evidence, acceptable to the Buyer, that each condition in clause 11.3 has been satisfied or irrevocably waived by Bluefen. Seller obligation at "all reasonable endeavours" or "best endeavours", with a Buyer-only waiver right and a long-stop. Delete the deemed-satisfaction language. Consider a price-protection mechanism (retention/escrow or specific indemnity) if Completion is to occur before clause 11.3 conditions are fully evidenced – but only with Amelia Frost's instruction.

### 3.2 Riverlark Bank facility (Clauses 2 / 7)
- **Playbook:** Current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion. A post-Completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking **plus** Amelia Frost approval.
- **Facts (Disclosure Letter para 3):** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; change-of-control clause 8.1; discharge clause 9.2; facility not repaid; no final discharge of security.
- **Departure:** Seller proposes a release "to be provided following Completion". This is a debt-free/cash-free deal: we would complete with AUD 3.2m of secured debt still on the Company, the bank holding security over assets we have just paid for, a change-of-control default live under clause 8.1, and the Seller holding the price. The "approximately" figure also suggests no current payout letter.
- **Pushback:** (a) Current payout letter from Riverlark dated not more than 2–3 business days before Completion, figure to be a line item in the funds flow deducted from the price. (b) Buyer pays Riverlark directly at Completion from the Completion payment. (c) Executed deeds of release/discharge of all security (and PPSR release undertakings) delivered at Completion, held in escrow pending payment. (d) Riverlark's written confirmation that clause 8.1 is waived or spent on repayment. Reject the post-Completion release. If the Seller cannot deliver releases at Completion, do not proceed on that basis without an irrevocable bank undertaking **and** Amelia Frost's written approval.

### 3.3 Funds flow and DD-005 bonuses
- **Playbook:** AUD 420,000 bonuses plus triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or Seller-funded; the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Facts (Disclosure Letter para 5):** AUD 420k conditional Completion bonuses; **not** in the draft funds flow; disclosure silent on payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs.
- **Departure:** The Seller's note says the bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" but simultaneously keeps them out of the funds flow. If they are not in the funds flow and not otherwise Seller-funded, the Company (i.e. the Buyer post-Completion) pays them. This is a transaction cost triggered by the Seller's sale and belongs with the Seller. The reference to "agreed price mechanics" should be rejected – nothing is agreed.
- **Pushback:** Treat DD-005 bonuses as Transaction Bonuses within the Debt/Transaction Costs definition: AUD 420,000 **plus** superannuation, payroll tax and any other employer on-costs (to be quantified by the Seller before signing), either (i) deducted from the price in the funds flow and paid by the Company at Completion out of Seller proceeds, or (ii) paid by the Seller directly with a Seller indemnity for any shortfall and on-costs. Require the Seller to confirm whether any additional retention or change-of-control payments exist beyond DD-005.

### 3.4 Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)
- These are disclosed as notification-only / assignment restriction only. We should not accept the Seller's characterisation without reading the clauses ourselves (the Seller's 1.4 reservation applies here too). **Action:** DD confirmation whether a share sale triggers either a landlord consent or a Mossvale change-of-control right; if either does, add to the Conditions/Completion deliverables. If not, require the notifications to be given pre-Completion with evidence.

## 4. Specific risk items

### 4.1 Ironquay IP (Clause 11.1)
- **Playbook:** Broaden the narrow indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- **Facts (Disclosure Letter para 4):** DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180k open; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in the data room; DD-010 is not bank verification.
- **Departure:** The Seller's indemnity covers only the SOW3 payment. The real exposure is not the AUD 180k – it is that the Company may not own the SOW3 deliverables at all until payment clears, and any loss from non-ownership (customer claims, re-development cost, inability to license) is uncapped by the payment amount.
- **Pushback:** (a) Pre-Completion cure: Seller to procure cleared payment of all SOW3 fees and deliver Ironquay's written receipt plus a confirmatory IP assignment of SOW3 Project Materials as a Completion deliverable. (b) Indemnity broadened to cover all Loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or any third-party claim to, the SOW3 Project Materials or any other Ironquay deliverable, including any further amounts Ironquay claims, not merely the SOW3 payment. (c) Indemnity outside Clause 12 limitations. (d) Neither side should assume the AUD 180k is correct – require a reconciled statement from Ironquay.

### 4.2 Export / privacy incident (DD-006; Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6)
- **Playbook:** Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- **Facts (Disclosure Letter para 6):** Download link sent to unintended external address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps); unknown whether accessed; investigation preliminary; no loss stated.
- **Departure:** Seller's cover note calls it "preliminary" and "not expected to be material" – but its own Disclosure Letter says the material cannot establish access, scope or notification requirement. "Not expected to be material" is a conclusion the Seller's own evidence does not support (nor contradict).
- **Pushback (without asserting a breach):** (a) Pre-Completion covenant to preserve all logs, link access records and correspondence, and to complete the investigation (including link revocation confirmation and access-log analysis) with written updates to the Buyer. (b) Bring-down of the disclosure at Completion. (c) Specific indemnity for Loss arising from the DD-006 incident (regulator action, notification costs, third-party claims), outside Clause 12 caps and time limits, with a specific indemnity period of at least six years. (d) Do not propose a price adjustment or quantify a demand – there is no basis for a number yet. (e) Warranty that no other similar incidents have occurred in the last three years.

### 4.3 Sandbar renewals (DD-008 / DD-011) – AUD 330,000
- **Playbook:** Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Facts (Disclosure Letter para 8):** Three related renewals of AUD 110k each; the disclosure does not say whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Departure:** Seller's cover note asserts "ordinary-course operating costs"; the Disclosure Letter expressly declines to say so. Mild inconsistency, not yet a dispute.
- **Pushback:** Do **not** propose a Debt classification or price deduction now. Instead request: renewal dates and terms, termination rights and notice periods, whether any amount is accrued or prepaid at the locked-box/Completion accounts date, and whether the three are a single commitment split or genuinely separate. Decide classification once answered. If they are accrued pre-Completion but unpaid, they belong in Working Capital/Debt under the completion mechanism; if genuinely forward-looking ordinary course, they do not.

### 4.4 Title (DD-012)
- **Playbook:** Independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; the DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- **Facts (Disclosure Letter para 10):** Title is evidenced by the Company's own share register; the Seller expressly notes the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Departure:** The Seller's note treats DD-012 as sufficient. A company's own register is maintained by the company (i.e. by the Seller's appointees) and is prima facie evidence only.
- **Pushback / DD actions:** (a) Current ASIC company extract showing Harbourglass as sole member and matching share capital. (b) PPSR search against the Company and against Harbourglass for security over the shares (Riverlark security in particular). (c) Copies of all share certificates, transfer history and board minutes approving the register entries. (d) Harbourglass's own constitutional documents and board/shareholder resolutions approving the sale (capacity and authority). (e) Full Fundamental Warranties (title, no encumbrances, capacity, authority, share capital, no options/convertibles) on the separate regime at 1.4 above.
